question: Identify the structure that controls the size of the pupil.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Iris.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** iris** controls the **size of the pupil** by adjusting its diameter through the contraction and dilation of its muscles, regulating the amount of light entering the eye.
 
• The iris is the colored part of the eye, with its color varying due to the amount and type of** pigment** present. This color can be blue, brown, green, etc.
 
• It consists of two sets of smooth muscles: the **sphincter pupillae** (which constricts the pupil) and the **dilator pupillae** (which dilates the pupil).
 
• The iris plays a** crucial** role in adapting to different lighting conditions by controlling pupil size, helping to protect the retina from excessive light, and improving vision in varying light conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitreous Humour:**

 
 
• A gel-like substance fills the space between the **lens** and the **retina**.
 
• It helps maintain the** eye’s shape **and provides a pathway for light to reach the retina.
 
• It does not play a role in controlling pupil size or light regulation.
 
 
 
• **Ciliary Muscles:**
 
 
• **Muscles** located around the lens of the eye.
 
• They control the shape of the lens for focusing on near and distant objects (accommodation).
 
• While **crucial for focusing**, they do not control pupil size.
 
 
 
• **Cornea:**
 
 
• The transparent, outer layer of the eye that covers the** iris **and** pupil**.
 
• It provides most of the eye's **optical power** by refracting light entering the eye.
 
• It does not control the size of the pupil; rather, it helps **focus light **on the retina.
